common.tagline: Vendor-neutral home for your AI agents

hero.title: One playbook. Every agent.
hero.subtitle: One vendor-neutral playbook for the whole job — skills, MCP servers, instructions, memory, and credentials your agent uses without seeing — deployed to Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Antigravity, and Hermes in one command.

whatIsPlaybook.title: What is a Playbook?
whatIsPlaybook.subtitle: A Playbook is the complete operating environment for an AI agent - everything it needs to work effectively, all in one place.
whatIsPlaybook.description: Think of it as your agent's portable work profile: a source of truth that travels with you across platforms and vendors.

persona.title: Persona
persona.subtitle: Personality & Style
persona.description: The agent's base personality, communication style, and system prompt. This defines HOW the agent behaves and responds.

skills.title: Skills
skills.subtitle: Knowledge & Capabilities
skills.description: Structured task definitions and knowledge the agent can use. Skills define WHAT the agent knows and can do — and can bundle files, or point at recordings of the task being performed, for agents that learn by watching.

mcp.title: MCP Servers
mcp.subtitle: Tools & Integrations
mcp.description: External tools and APIs the agent can access via Model Context Protocol. Code execution happens at the agent itself - these are the connections.

canvas.title: Canvas
canvas.subtitle: Working Documents
canvas.description: Structured markdown documents that serve as the agent's workspace. Notes, drafts, project files - persistent documents the agent can read and write.

memory.title: Memory

memory.description: Key-value storage for remembering facts, preferences, and state across sessions. The agent's long-term memory.

switchPlatform.question: Want to switch from ChatGPT to Gemini, but can't take your memory and conversations with you?
switchPlatform.answer: Your playbook travels with you. All personas, skills, and memories are stored platform-independently - just point your new AI to your playbook URL.

portableSkills.question: Built amazing skills in Claude, but want to use them in other platforms too?
portableSkills.answer: Skills in your playbook work everywhere. Export in Anthropic format, OpenAPI for GPTs, or any other format - your investment isn't locked to one vendor.

missingActions.question: Love Grok but miss ChatGPT's custom actions and integrations?
missingActions.answer: Define your MCP servers and tools in your playbook - any AI that supports tool use can access them, regardless of platform.

teamConsistency.question: Your team uses different AI platforms, but needs consistent behavior?
teamConsistency.answer: Share a playbook URL. Everyone's AI - whether Claude, GPT, or local LLM - follows the same guidelines and has access to the same skills.

futureProof.question: Worried about being locked into today's AI platform?
futureProof.answer: AgentPlaybooks is open source with standard formats, and already ready for agents with a body: a skill can carry demonstrations — timestamped recordings of the task, in the order a robot performs them.

localLlm.question: Running local LLMs but want the same capabilities as cloud services?
localLlm.answer: Point your local model to your playbook. Same skills, same persona, same memory - just running on your hardware.

## Build and test

## Conventions

explore.heroNote: Your knowledge stays portable. Your agent does the work.

explore.casesTitle: Same AI. A better starting point.

explore.contextNote: Only the relevant material, not your entire knowledge base.

explore.starterNote: These public, first-party starters are in English and contain generic instructions. Make a private copy before adding your project details. The scenarios above illustrate how to customize them.

handoff.title: Pick up a project
handoff.headline: A new chat shouldn’t mean a blank slate.
handoff.description: Return to a project after a week, or switch to another assistant, without reconstructing every decision.
handoff.prompt: “Pick up the Northstar portal. What should we do next?”
handoff.situation: You have opened a new session. The previous conversation isn’t in its context.

context.goal: Ship accessible onboarding for the customer portal.
context.skill: Separate confirmed work, open questions and next actions.
context.memory: Email-link login was chosen. Staging works; production is still unchecked.

handoff.resultTitle: A handoff you can act on

results.one: Current state: staging login is recorded as working. Production remains unverified.
results.two: Next checks: email delivery, expired links and keyboard navigation.
results.three: Ask for the production environment and permission before making changes.

research.title: Turn research into a decision
research.headline: Keep the reasoning, not just the answer.
research.description: Use a repeatable research method and saved constraints to build a brief someone can challenge and update.
research.prompt: “Compare these two issue trackers for our team. What’s missing before we choose?”
research.situation: You provide two source documents. The assistant should not fill their gaps with invented facts.

context.goal: Find a tracker for a small team that needs data export.
context.skill: Compare evidence, cite supplied sources and separate unknowns.
context.memory: Export is required. Budget approval and SSO requirements are still open.

results.one: A comparison of claims in the supplied documents, with source references.
results.two: A gap list: verify export coverage, final price and the required SSO plan.
results.three: A conditional recommendation, with the assumptions that could change it.

review.title: Review a change
review.headline: Make your standards part of the review.
review.description: Bring project rules and past decisions into a code review instead of repeating the same checklist each time.
review.prompt: “Review this API caching change. What must we verify before release?”
review.situation: Your coding agent can inspect the diff and run checks when its tools and permissions allow it.

context.goal: Reduce response time without exposing private data.
context.skill: Trace access boundaries, cache keys, invalidation and failure paths.
context.memory: Public and private responses must stay isolated. Measure before claiming a speedup.

results.one: Inspect whether cache keys distinguish every relevant access scope.
results.two: Check permission changes, stale entries and anonymous versus signed-in requests.
results.three: Report verified results, remaining risks and the measurements still needed.

memory.question: How is this different from chat history?
memory.answer: A playbook stores chosen instructions, skills and saved facts outside a single conversation. It does not automatically remember every chat. Your assistant needs to read the relevant context and explicitly save anything worth keeping.

execution.question: Does AgentPlaybooks run the work for me?
execution.answer: Your AI client and its connected tools execute the work. AgentPlaybooks supplies reusable context and configuration. It does not turn a saved instruction into a scheduled job or grant your assistant extra permissions.

privacy.question: Where do my project details belong?
privacy.answer: In your own private playbook. Public starters are examples anyone may read. Copy one before adding project information, check who has access, and keep credentials in the dedicated secret-management features.

tools.question: Should I use MCP, skills or the API?
tools.answer: Use the route your client supports best. MCP offers structured tools inside a conversation; skills provide reusable instructions; the CLI and API suit file-based or automated workflows. Small, targeted reads matter more than the name of the connection.

selfHostSecurity.title: Keep control. Keep the evidence.
selfHostSecurity.intro: Self-host with encrypted credentials, scoped access, and an audit trail you can inspect, verify, and export.

secrets.title: Credentials with boundaries
secrets.description: AES-256-GCM encryption with per-user derived keys. Inject credentials server-side, enforce expiry, and restrict the destination hosts a secret can reach.

access.title: Separate access by role
access.description: Give agents scoped API keys and reviewers read-only auditor access. Enable private-instance mode when every playbook must stay private.

audit.title: Trace changes and credential use
audit.description: Record vault operations, federated calls, configuration changes, and memory/canvas writes. Keep outcomes and actor metadata without copying secret values or content bodies.

evidence.title: Verify and export the trail
evidence.description: Per-playbook SHA-256 hash chains and protected append-only history survive playbook deletion. Verify from the API or CLI, and export JSONL or CSV for review.

forwarding.title: Fit your audit operations
forwarding.description: Optionally forward application audit events to a signed HTTPS SIEM webhook or Node syslog. Configure retention and schedule purges with checkpoints that preserve chain verification.

operations.title: Run on your infrastructure
operations.description: Use mTLS through a trusted TLS proxy on your own deployment. Encrypted backup and restore tooling, with restore drills, helps you plan and verify recovery.

selfHostSecurity.operationsNote: Inspect the security documentation for configuration and limits, plus CodeQL checks, CycloneDX SBOMs, and signed SBOM evidence. SIEM forwarding is optional and best-effort; retention runs on your schedule.
